audit.why: Emerald+ headline 50.3% over 656 games; EVEN at 6/10 is a fair reading of a coinflip lane.

audit.whatIsWrong: The layers disagree on the shape. The content chart and the packet levelChart read Skill / Aurora / Skill / Aurora / Skill / Skill / Rumble, while CHAMP_FULL.phases reads Skill / Rumble / Rumble / Skill / Skill / Rumble / Rumble. Level 2 is the clearest inversion: the full layer awards it to Rumble, the chart and both content paragraphs award it to Aurora.
audit.why: The content reasoning is right and comes from the kit — at 2 she has a ranged 900-range Twofold Hex and a hop, and Rumble's Flamespitter needs her to stand still. Level 2 is not a Rumble level. Overall EVEN at 6/10 is correct for 50.3%, so only the row-level sides are wrong.
audit.corrected: phases[1].side set to Aurora. The remaining side mismatches are outside the length band and are listed in notes.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike treats 6 as purely Rumble's ultimate spike and never mentions that Aurora also gets Between Worlds. The 4-5 spike attributes her peak entirely to kiting and omits the sustain that actually makes the poke war unwinnable.
audit.why: Between Worlds is 140/120/100 and, past the shockwave, leaves a zone Aurora alone can teleport across — that is a second escape stacked on top of Across the Veil, and it changes how a level-6 all-in resolves. Spirit Abjuration heals her off the spirits her own spells and attacks exorcise, so Rumble's chip damage is partly refunded during exactly the 4-5 window the spike describes.
audit.corrected: Both spikes restated with Between Worlds and Spirit Abjuration named, and Across the Veil's 22-second rank-1 cooldown given.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer calls her defining ability 'Twofold Hunt' in fifteen places and glosses it as 'Her escape / (Blink)'. Both halves are wrong: the ability is Twofold Hex, and it is her Q poke missile, not an escape. Her escape is Across the Veil (W). Separately, the content layer invents a root — 'before she lands her root', 'bait your W shield with a root combo', 'her root burst' — and Aurora has no root in any ability description. And Twofold Hex's actual mechanic, the one that decides trades, is never mentioned: the missile curses, and the recast drags every active curse back toward her, damaging anyone the return path crosses.
audit.why: The kit file is the authority on names. Twofold Hex, Across the Veil, The Weirding, Between Worlds and Spirit Abjuration are the real five. Telling a Rumble player to all-in when 'her escape' is down while pointing at her 9-second poke Q instead of her 22-second W is advice that gets him killed. The invented root makes him pre-shield against a threat that does not exist rather than against the curse return, which is the burst that is actually coming.
audit.corrected: Twofold Hunt replaced with the correct ability in every reachable string, the escape re-attributed to Across the Veil, the root removed, and the curse-recast mechanic written into the trading and Do-not lines.

audit.whatIsWrong: No Aurora cooldown appears anywhere, and the one cooldown the reader is told to track is the wrong ability.
audit.why: Across the Veil is 22/21/20/19/18 — an enormous window at rank 1 and the actual punish. Twofold Hex is 9/8.5/8/7.5/7, The Weirding 15/14/13/12/11, Between Worlds 140/120/100.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into the cooldown breakdown, the Do, and the 4-5 spike.

audit.whatIsWrong: The itemization row lists no Grievous Wounds despite Aurora having passive healing.
audit.why: Spirit Abjuration's description is explicit — spirits exorcised by her spells and attacks follow her and heal her. Against Rumble's chip-damage pattern that heal compounds, and _missing-interactions.json flags this matchup for anti-heal timing. This is the one anti-heal flag in my slice that Riot's own text supports.
audit.corrected: Oblivion Orb added to the item path ahead of the second item.

notes: The 'Twofold Hunt' fabrication is doubly wrong — the name does not exist and the ability it points at is her poke Q, not the escape the text tells you to track. This is the same class of error as the Brand and Cassiopeia calibration cases, and it is worth grepping the whole repo for 'Twofold Hunt' since the string looks auto-generated rather than hand-written. The invented Aurora 'root' in the content layer is a second fabrication in the same matchup. I left the 'early' and 'mid' paragraphs alone: they lean on the same 'E blink' shorthand, which is defensible because The Weirding really does hop her backward, but 'mid' also contains 'her root burst', which is not defensible. Rewriting 'mid' inside plus-or-minus 10 percent while removing the root and keeping the paragraph's argument intact needs more room than the band allows, so I flagged it here rather than shipping a cramped version. Note also that The Equalizer is not terrain — Riot calls it a wall of flames that damages and slows — so 'no safe exit from the burning wall' was reframed as damage on her landing spot.
